title: UNIT 2: PHYSICAL QUANTITIES
notes:
✓ Physical quantity → Measurable property expressed by a numerical value and a unit.

✓ Measurement → Comparison of an unknown quantity with a known standard unit.

title: 2.1 SCALES, STANDARDS, UNITS & PREFIXES
notes:
✓ Scale → Markings or values used for measuring a quantity.

✓ Standard → Fixed reference used to make measurements consistent and comparable.

✓ SI (International System of Units) → Internationally accepted system of measurement.

◆ SEVEN SI BASE QUANTITIES
✓ Length → Meter (m).
✓ Mass → Kilogram (kg).
✓ Time → Second (s).
✓ Temperature → Kelvin (K).
✓ Electric current → Ampere (A).
✓ Amount of substance → Mole (mol).
✓ Luminous intensity → Candela (cd).

title: 2.1.1 MEASUREMENT SCALES
notes:
✓ Nominal → Classifies objects into categories.
✓ Ordinal → Arranges values by order or rank.
✓ Interval → Has equal intervals but no true zero.
✓ Ratio → Has equal intervals with a true zero; allows meaningful mathematical operations.

✓ Most physical measurements → Use ratio scales.

title: 2.1.2 SCIENTIFIC NOTATION & SIGNIFICANT FIGURES
notes:
✓ Scientific notation → Expresses very large or small numbers as:
x × 10ⁿ

✓ Significant figures → Meaningful digits in a measured value.

✓ Non-zero digits → Are significant.
✓ Zeros between non-zero digits → Are significant.
✓ Final zeros in a decimal number → Are significant.

✓ Multiplication/division → Give the answer with the same number of significant figures as the value having the fewest significant figures.

title: 2.1.3 SI PREFIXES
notes:
✓ SI prefixes → Represent multiples or fractions of SI units.

✓ Tera (T) → 10¹².
✓ Giga (G) → 10⁹.
✓ Mega (M) → 10⁶.
✓ Kilo (k) → 10³.
✓ Hecto (h) → 10².
✓ Deka (da) → 10¹.
✓ Deci (d) → 10⁻¹.
✓ Centi (c) → 10⁻².
✓ Milli (m) → 10⁻³.
✓ Micro (µ) → 10⁻⁶.
✓ Nano (n) → 10⁻⁹.
✓ Pico (p) → 10⁻¹².

title: 2.2 MEASUREMENT AND SAFETY
notes:
✓ Measurement → Has three key elements:
◆ Physical quantity being measured.
◆ Measuring instrument.
◆ Standard unit.

✓ Every measurement → Contains a numerical value and a unit.

title: 2.2.1 MEASURING LENGTH
notes:
✓ Length → Distance between two points.
✓ SI unit → Meter (m).
✓ Common units → Kilometer (km), centimeter (cm), millimeter (mm).

✓ Measuring instruments → Are selected according to the size and nature of the object.

title: 2.2.2 MEASURING MASS
notes:
✓ Mass → Amount of matter contained in a body.
✓ SI unit → Kilogram (kg).
✓ Common units → Gram (g), milligram (mg), tonne.

✓ Beam balance → Scientific instrument used to measure mass.

title: 2.2.3 MEASURING TIME
notes:
✓ Time → Interval between two events.
✓ SI unit → Second (s).
✓ Other units → Minute (min), hour (h), day, month and year.

✓ Time → Can be measured using clocks and other time-measuring devices.

title: 2.3 CLASSIFICATION OF PHYSICAL QUANTITIES
notes:
✓ Physical quantities → Are classified as:

◆ Fundamental and derived quantities.
◆ Scalar and vector quantities.

title: 2.3.1 FUNDAMENTAL PHYSICAL QUANTITIES
notes:
✓ Fundamental quantities → Are basic quantities that are not expressed in terms of other physical quantities.

✓ Length → m.
✓ Mass → kg.
✓ Time → s.
✓ Temperature → K.
✓ Electric current → A.
✓ Amount of substance → mol.
✓ Luminous intensity → cd.

title: 2.3.2 DERIVED PHYSICAL QUANTITIES
notes:
✓ Derived quantities → Are obtained from fundamental quantities.

✓ Area → m².
✓ Volume → m³.
✓ Speed → Distance/time → m/s.
✓ Density → Mass/volume → kg/m³.
✓ Acceleration → Change in velocity/time → m/s².
✓ Force → Mass × acceleration → N.
✓ Work → Force × displacement → J.
✓ Pressure → Force/area → Pa.

title: 2.3.3 SCALAR AND VECTOR QUANTITIES
notes:
✓ Scalar quantity → Has magnitude only.

◆ Examples
✓ Mass • time • distance • speed • temperature • energy • pressure.

✓ Vector quantity → Has both magnitude and direction.

◆ Examples
✓ Displacement • velocity • acceleration • force • momentum.

✓ Example → 50 km/h east → 50 km/h is the magnitude; east is the direction.

title: 2.4 UNIT CONVERSION
notes:
✓ Unit conversion → Changing a measurement from one unit to another unit of the same physical quantity.

✓ Conversion factor → Used so that the original unit cancels and the required unit remains.

title: 2.4.3 TIME CONVERSION
notes:
✓ 1 min = 60 s.
✓ 1 h = 60 min = 3600 s.
✓ 1 day = 24 h.
✓ 1 week = 7 days.
✓ 1 year = 365.25 days.

title: UNIT 2 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
◆ PHYSICAL QUANTITY
✓ Numerical value + unit.

◆ MEASUREMENT
✓ Comparison with a standard.

◆ SI
✓ International System of Units.

◆ FUNDAMENTAL
✓ Basic quantities.

◆ DERIVED
✓ Combinations of fundamental quantities.

◆ SCALAR
✓ Magnitude only.

◆ VECTOR
✓ Magnitude + direction.

◆ KEY FORMULAS
✓ Speed = distance/time.
✓ Density = mass/volume.
✓ Acceleration = change in velocity/time.
✓ Force = mass × acceleration.
✓ Work = force × displacement.
✓ Pressure = force/area.

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Always write the numerical answer together with its correct unit.
